# Where Plūtō works now: the myths behind the markets
If the stories are true in the way that matters, they should show up in the world without being invoked. **Plūtō** shows up constantly.

Plūtō's Roman myths retell the Greek cycle with a merchant's accent: the underworld as a treasury as much as a tribunal.

The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) — which maps every flagship temple to the industries its archetype demonstrably resonates with, each match argued and open to challenge — seats this temple in **3 industries**. This file reads those seats the way they were earned: through the myths.
## At a Glance

- **Temple:** Plūtō
- **Pantheon:** Roman
- **Domain of influence:** Underworld, Wealth, the Dead
- **Pattern seats:** 3
- **Sectors touched:** Society & Spirit · Energy & Natural World · Commerce & Governance
- **Strongest seat:** Funerary & Memorial Services
- **Series:** The Resonance Files, No. 195 of 271
## The Myth at Work

**Proserpina in the Meadow.** Ovid tells the Roman version of the oldest underworld story: Plūtō rose through the earth of Henna's meadow as Proserpina gathered flowers, and carried her down through the lake's opening to be his queen.  Cerēs searched the world with torches; the famine followed her grief; and the settlement — half the year above, half below — made the seasons. — hold that image; the industries below are where it goes to work.

**Plūtus the Giver.** Under the name Plūtus he was the benign twin: the wealth that comes from under the earth — grain, metal, the harvest itself.  Aristophanes' comedy made him a blind old man who, healed, gives riches to the just; Rome's poets used him for the moral that wealth, like the grave, is no respecter of persons. — that is not just a story. It is a business model, four thousand years early.
## The Seats

Each of these is argued in the atlas with a weight and a why-line. What the atlas cannot fit in one line is the whole myth — so here is each seat with its story restored.

### Funerary & Memorial Services

*Funeral care, memorials, and legacy services. (Sector: Society & Spirit)*

*The underworld itself; the oldest address of the dead.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

### Mining & Natural Resources

*Extraction, minerals, and subterranean wealth. (Sector: Energy & Natural World)*

*The Rich One below — ore, wealth, and the deep.* — the atlas stops there, out of discipline. The myth keeps going: the function Plūtō performs in the stories is precisely the function this industry sells.

### Finance, Wealth & Commerce

*Banking, investment, and commercial enterprise. (Sector: Commerce & Governance)*

*Plutus the giver; wealth from the earth personified.* Swap the costume and the sentence is indistinguishable from the myth. That is what a resonance seat means.

Read the myth again after the seats and it stops sounding ancient: Plūtō's Roman myths retell the Greek cycle with a merchant's accent: the underworld as a treasury as much as a tribunal. The age changed. The work did not.
## The Method, Stated Plainly

None of this is numerology. A seat exists only where the match can be argued from the deity's documented domains and deeds — weighted, published, and falsifiable. The full derivation, the weights, and the challenge process are public on the [methodology page](/patterns/methodology/). If a seat in this file reads wrong, the atlas itself tells you how to prove it — and the correction becomes part of the record.
## For the Ones Who Work There

If you work in funerary & memorial services, mining & natural resources, or any trade this temple holds a seat in, this is the honest version of what a placement means: your industry beside the story it has been re-telling all along — on the temple floor itself, before an audience that came specifically to read it. The [patron tier](/sites/pluto/patron/) and the [advertising terms](/terms/advertising/) describe the mechanics; the resonance above describes the fit. The story is the pitch; the seats are just where it already works.
